3. Creative Builds ​

3.1 Smart Beckoning Cat ​

3.1.1 Introduction ​

This is a smart beckoning cat capable of automated welcoming. Upon powering on, the device continuously captures the scene ahead. When the camera detects a face, the servo drives the beckoning cat to wave its hand, while the voice module broadcasts "Hello, welcome." Just like a warm receptionist in a store, it automatically completes the entire welcoming interaction.

3.1.2 Learning Objectives ​

  1. Understand the 270° block servo and the WonderLLM module, mastering coordinated control using the micro:bit expansion board.
  2. Comprehend the logic of facial recognition and voice control, learning to implement face-triggered voice broadcasting and automated waving.

3.1.3 Assembly Guide ​

3.1.4 Mode Switching ​

This model requires the offline vision function. If the offline vision function mode has been entered, skip this step and proceed directly to the wiring guide. Otherwise, refer to 4.6.1 Firmware Update to re-flash the corresponding firmware.

3.1.4 Wiring Guide ​

  • Insert the WonderLLM module cable into port 4 of the micro:bit expansion board.
  • Insert the 270° block servo cable into port S1 of the micro:bit expansion board, ensuring the yellow wire of the servo is inserted into the white pin of S1.

NOTE

For the first course involving the block servo, remove the building blocks from the servo first, and upload the program of this course to the micro:bit. Then, turn on the power switch of the micro:bit expansion board and wait for the block servo to rotate to its initial position of 0 degrees before reinstalling the building blocks. This step can be skipped if the servo reset program has been executed previously.

3.1.6 Programming ​

(1) Program Flowchart ​

(3) Core Blocks Analysis ​

Instruction BlockCategoryFunction Description
Define or get a variable used to store data
Assign a value to a custom variable
Initialize the DaDabit module to prepare for subsequent use
Initialize the WonderLLM interface to establish module communication
Switch the working mode of WonderLLM, supporting voice interaction, color recognition, and face recognition modes
Detect whether a face is recognized and return a boolean result
Control the angle and execution time of the 270° servo on the specified port
Play the preset voice broadcast content in the WonderEcho module

(3) Complete Program ​

Program link: https://makecode.microbit.org/_HJPcTaJzALHt. Click Edit Code in the upper-right corner of the page to download the complete program.

3.1.7 Downloading the Program ​

3.1.8 Project Extensions ​

When a face is recognized, the onboard RGB LED is set to yellow and the micro:bit dot matrix display shows Hi, synchronously triggering the light, pattern, sound, and waving action to enhance the welcoming atmosphere.

3.2 Color Scanner ​

3.2.1 Introduction ​

This is a color scanner capable of color recognition. Upon powering on, it continuously detects the color of objects in front of it. When the sensor identifies a specific color, the on-board RGB LED of the controller synchronously illuminates in the matching color. Working like a precise color detector, it provides direct visual feedback of the recognition results.

3.2.2 Learning Objectives ​

  1. Master the micro:bit expansion board's onboard RGB LED and the WonderLLM offline color recognition feature, understanding multi-module coordinated control.
  2. Comprehend the interaction logic between color recognition and visual feedback, learning to display identified colors synchronously.

3.3 Adjustable Mixer ​

3.3.1 Introduction ​

This is an adjustable mixer featuring voice-controlled speed regulation. It remains in a standby stationary state after powering on. Upon receiving a voice command, the servo starts the mixing mechanism and switches between three speed levels, acting as a smart kitchen assistant that adjusts the mixing speed on demand.

3.3.2 Learning Objectives ​

  1. Recognize the 270° servo and the WonderLLM Online LLM module, and master the multi-device coordinated control method of the micro:bit expansion board.
  2. Comprehend the semantic analysis of the large AI model and the principles of servo speed regulation, mastering voice-controlled three-level speed changes.

3.3.3 Assembly Guide ​

3.3.4 Mode Switching ​

This model requires the Online LLM. If the Online LLM mode has been entered, skip this step and proceed directly to the wiring guide. Otherwise, refer to 4.5.10 Firmware Update to re-flash the corresponding firmware.

3.3.4 Wiring Guide ​

  • Insert the WonderLLM module cable into port 4 of the micro:bit expansion board.

  • Insert the 360° block servo cable into port S1 of the micro:bit expansion board, ensuring the yellow wire of the servo is inserted into the white pin of S1.

    As shown below:

3.3.6 Programming ​

(1) Program Flowchart ​

(3) Core Blocks Analysis ​

Instruction BlockCategoryFunction Description
Loop execution of the internal program at set millisecond intervals
Compare whether the preceding and succeeding values are equal and return a boolean result
Compare whether two strings are identical and return a boolean result
Define or get a variable used to store data
Assign a value to a custom variable
Initialize the DaDabit module to prepare for subsequent use
Initialize the WonderLLM interface to establish module communication
Configure custom tool parameters that can be called by the ai module
Synchronize mcp tool configuration information with the ai module
Read the running data sent back after the ai module calls the tool
Extract the corresponding numeric value from the target dictionary based on the specified key and return it
Inform the ai module that a single tool call process has ended
Control the angle and execution time of the 270° block servo on the specified port
Determine whether the target text contains the specified character and return a boolean result

MCP Parameter Configuration ​

  • Tool Name: self.robot.setMode

  1. Tool Description: You are a blender with three modes to choose from. Parameter description: Gear range: 0 to 3, returns 0 when stopping, returns 1 for first gear, returns 2 for second gear, and returns 3 for third gear.

  2. AI Module Return Parameters: [["mode", "int", "0", "0", "3"]]

NOTE

The field name is mode, integer type, the first 0 is the default value, the second 0 is the minimum value, and 3 is the maximum value.

  1. Block until call is completed: true

  2. Return data to AI Module: false

  3. Function: This MCP configuration defines the hardware speed regulation tool for the AI module. It allows the AI to issue gear commands from 0 to 3 to control the start, stop, and speed changes of the blender. The program will wait for the gear execution to complete during the call, and there is no need to send running data back to the AI.

(4) Complete Program ​

Program link: https://makecode.microbit.org/_Jar64WW2Xipj. Click Edit Code in the upper-right corner of the page to download the complete program.

3.3.8 Project Extensions ​

Without modifying the original three-level speed regulation logic, add green, yellow, and red RGB LED indications corresponding to speed levels 1, 2, and 3, respectively, to provide visual gear prompts.

  • Insert the WonderLLM module cable into port 3 of the micro:bit expansion board.

​ As shown below:

3.8.6 Programming ​

(1) Program Flowchart ​

(3) Core Blocks Analysis ​

Instruction BlockCategoryFunction Description
Define or get a variable used to store data
Assign a value to a custom variable
Initialize the DaDabit module to prepare for subsequent use
Initialize the WonderLLM interface to establish module communication
Configure custom tool parameters that can be called by the ai module
Synchronize mcp tool configuration information with the ai module
Read the running data sent back after the ai module calls the tool
Inform the ai module that a single tool call process has ended
Extract the corresponding numeric value from the target dictionary based on the specified key and return it
Control the running direction and speed of the 360° block servo on the specified port
Determine whether the target text contains the specified character

MCP Parameter Configuration ​

  • Tool Name: self.robot.setCook

  1. Tool Description: You are a Chef Bot. The parameters are as follows: Switch: 0 or 1. When turned on, it returns 1; when turned off, it returns 0.

  2. AI Module Return Parameters: [["cook", "int", "0", "0", "1"]]

NOTE

The field name is cook, integer type, the first 0 is the default value, the second 0 is the minimum value, and 1 is the maximum value.

  1. Block until call is completed: true

  2. Return data to AI Module: false

  3. Function: This MCP configuration defines the switch control tool of the Chef Bot for the AI module. It allows the AI to send a command of 0 or 1 to control the start and stop of the Chef Bot, where turning it on returns 1 and turning it off returns 0. The program will wait for the operation to complete during the call, and there is no need to send extra running data back to the AI.

(4) Complete Program ​

Program link: https://makecode.microbit.org/_L7xRHq7j22x6. Click Edit Code in the upper-right corner of the page to download the complete program.

3.16.6 Programming ​

(1) Program Flowchart ​

(3) Core Blocks Analysis ​

Instruction BlockCategoryFunction Description
Compare whether two values are equal and return a boolean result
Define or get a variable used to store data
Assign a value to a custom variable
Initialize the DaDabit module to prepare for subsequent use
Initialize the WonderLLM interface to establish module communication
Configure custom tool parameters that can be called by the ai module
Synchronize mcp tool configuration information with the ai module
Read the running data sent back after the ai module calls the tool
Extract the corresponding numeric value from the target dictionary based on the specified key and return it
Inform the ai module that a single tool call process has ended
Control the running direction and speed of the 360° block servo on the specified port
Determine whether the target text contains the specified character

MCP Parameter Configuration ​

  • Tool Name: self.robot.setMusic

  1. Tool Description: You can control the start and stop of the drumming. The parameters are as follows: 1 is returned when starting the drumming, and 0 is returned when stopping.

  2. AI Module Return Parameters: [["music", "int", "0", "0", "1"]]

NOTE

The field name is music, integer type, the first 0 is the default value, the second 0 is the minimum value, and 1 is the maximum value.

  1. Block until call is completed: true

  2. Return data to AI Module: false

  3. Function: This MCP configuration defines the switch control tool of the Rhythm Drummer for the AI module. It allows the AI to send a command of 0 or 1 to control the start and stop of the drumming action, where starting returns 1 and stopping returns 0. The program will wait for the operation to complete during the call, and there is no need to send extra running data back to the AI.

Define or obtain variables used to store interaction data

Read the detected distance from the ultrasonic sensor and return the measurement in centimeters
Determine whether the target text contains the specified character content
Convert data formats like numbers or booleans into standard text format

(3) MCP Parameter Configuration ​

  • Tool Name: self.robot.setDistance

  1. Tool Description: Data can be obtained from the ultrasonic sensor without specifying parameters. After issuing an instruction, a list will be returned to you, with the first item being the distance from the object. The unit is in centimeters.

  2. AIModule Return Parameters: [["setDistance","string"]]

    NOTE

    The field name is setDistance, of string type.

  3. Whether to block until the call is completed: true

  4. Whether there is data returned to the AIModule: true

  5. Function: This MCP configuration defines the ultrasonic ranging tool for the AI module. It allows the AI to obtain object distance data in centimeters from the ultrasonic sensor without issuing parameters. The returned result is a list where the first item is the distance value. The program will wait for the data reading to complete during the call and return the ranging result to the AI module for subsequent decisions.

  • Tool Name: self.robot.launch

  1. Tool Description: It is necessary to control the thrower to be called during launch, returning parameter 1 when launching and parameter 0 when not launching. When the distance range of the object is between 15-20 centimeters, it can be launched, otherwise it will not be launched.

  2. AIModule Return Parameters: [["launch","int","0","1"]]

    NOTE

    The field name is launch, of integer type, where the default value is 0 and the minimum value is 1.

  3. Whether to block until the call is completed: true

  4. Whether there is data returned to the AIModule: false

  5. Function: This MCP configuration defines the Catapult Car launch control tool for the AI module. It allows the AI to issue a 0 or 1 command to control whether the Catapult Car executes the launch, returning 1 when launching and 0 when not launching. Launch is only permitted when the object distance is within the range of 15 to 20 centimeters. Otherwise, it will not be executed. 3.29 Smart Knight ​

3.29.1 Introduction ​

This is a smart knight robot capable of charging on command. Upon powering on, it enters a standby state. The WonderLLM large model supports controlling the knight to move forward, backward, left, or right using voice commands. During a forward sprint, the right arm is raised. When the ultrasonic sensor detects an obstacle, its left arm is raised, and the robot reverses. When the path is clear, the RGB lights glow green, and it tracks lines. When an obstacle is detected, the lights turn red and an alarm is triggered. Like a brave mechanical knight, it uses smart perception and voice commands to complete line-tracking and obstacle avoidance tasks.

3.29.2 Learning Objectives ​

  1. Understand dual 360° block motors, dual 270° block servos, the ultrasonic sensor, the 4-channel line follower sensor, and the large AI model, mastering coordinated wiring and programming for multiple components.
  2. Master the control logic of voice-activated movement, servo arm actions, and ultrasonic audio-visual warnings combined with line following.

3.29.3 Assembly Guide ​

3.29.4 Mode Switching ​

This model requires the use of the Online LLM Mode. If the online LLM mode is already active, this step can be skipped to proceed directly to the wiring guide. Otherwise, please refer to Firmware Switching to re-burn the corresponding firmware.

3.29.5 Wiring Guide ​

  • Connect the WonderLLM module to port 4 of the micro:bit expansion board.

  • Connect the glowing ultrasonic sensor to port 6 of the micro:bit expansion board.

  • Connect the 4-channel line follower sensor to port 3 of the micro:bit expansion board.

  • Connect the left 360° block servo to port S1 of the micro:bit expansion board, ensuring the yellow wire of the servo is inserted into the white pin of S1.

  • Connect the right 360° block servo to port S2 of the micro:bit expansion board, ensuring the yellow wire of the servo is inserted into the white pin of S2.

  • Connect the 270° block servo controlling the shield to port S4 of the micro:bit expansion board, ensuring the yellow wire of the servo is inserted into the white pin of S4.

  • Connect the 270° block servo controlling the right hand to port S5 of the micro:bit expansion board, ensuring the yellow wire of the servo is inserted into the white pin of S5.

    As shown in the following image:

NOTE

Before the first lesson involving the block servo, remove the building blocks from the left and right servos and upload the program for this lesson to the micro:bit. Then turn on the power switch of the micro:bit expansion board and wait for all block servos to rotate to the initial position of 0 degrees before reinstalling the corresponding building blocks. This step can be skipped if the servo reset program has been executed previously.

3.29.6 Programming ​

(1) Mode 1 Voice Controlled Movement ​

  • Program Flowchart ​

  • Core Block Analysis ​

BlockCategoryDescription
Define or obtain variables used to store data
Assign values to custom variables
Initialize the DaDabit module to prepare for subsequent use
Initialize the WonderLLM interface and establish the module communication connection
Configure custom function tool parameters callable by the ai module
Synchronize mcp tool configuration information to the ai module
Read the running data returned after the ai module calls a tool
Extract the corresponding numeric value from the target dictionary based on the specified key and return it
Inform the ai module that the single tool call process has ended
Control the 360° block servo with the specified id to run continuously in the set rotation direction and speed
Determine whether the target text contains the specified characters

  • MCP Tool Parameter Configuration ​

  • Tool Name: self.robot.setMove

  1. Tool Description: You are a robot that can move forward, backward, turn left, and turn right. Parameter description: 1.Movement direction: return 1 when moving forward, return 2 when moving backward, return 3 when turning left, and return 4 when turning right; 2. Movement time: measured in milliseconds, default value is 2 seconds.

  2. AIModule Return Parameters: [["robot","string"], ["move", "int", "0", "0", "4"], ["time","int","2000","0","10000"]]

NOTE

  • The field name is robot, of string type

  • The field name is move, of integer type, where the first 0 is the default value, the second 0 is the minimum value, and 4 is the maximum value

  • The field name is time, of integer type, where the default value is 2000, the minimum value is 0, and the maximum value is 10000

  1. Whether to block until the call is completed: true

  2. Whether there is data returned to the AIModule: false

  3. Function: This MCP configuration defines the movement control tool of the smart knight robot for the AI module. It allows the AI to issue direction commands, including forward, backward, left turn, and right turn, returning 1, 2, 3, or 4, respectively, and a movement duration in milliseconds, with a default of 2000 and a range of 0 to 10000, to control the robot's movement. The program will wait for the movement to complete during the call, and there is no need to send additional operation data back to the AI.

  • Complete Program ​

3.30 Smart Avoidance Car ​

3.30.1 Introduction ​

This is a smart avoidance car capable of cruising on command. Upon powering on, it enters a standby state. The WonderLLM large model supports voice control for moving forward, backward, left, or right. It can follow black lines stably. After stopping, the servo drives the ultrasonic probe to swing left, front, and right to scan the distance of obstacles. Like a vigilant scout, it uses keen environmental awareness and flexible motion control to complete line following and obstacle avoidance tasks.

3.30.2 Learning Objectives ​

  1. Understand the 360° block motors, 270° scanning servo, ultrasonic sensor, 4-channel line follower sensor, and the WonderLLM large AI model, mastering multi-device wiring and coordinated programming.
  2. Master three types of functional logic: line-tracking cruise, servo scanning distance measurement, and voice-controlled mobility.

3.31 Tank Clawbot ​

3.31.1 Introduction ​

This is a multifunctional tank clawbot capable of working on command. Upon powering on, it enters a standby state. The WonderLLM large model supports voice control for moving forward, backward, left, or right. During line following, when the ultrasonic sensor detects an obstacle within 20 cm, it automatically halts line following and executes claw grabbing and placing sequences. Like an all-round engineering assistant, it uses voice commands to complete line following and grabbing tasks.

3.31.2 Learning Objectives ​

  1. Understand 360° block motors, the 270° grabbing servo, the ultrasonic sensor, the 4-channel line follower sensor, and the large AI model, mastering coordinated wiring and programming for multiple components.
  2. Master controlling tracked movement via voice, comprehending ultrasonic distance thresholds to automate line-tracking cruise and claw grabbing.

3.32 Smart Tank Car ​

3.32.1 Introduction ​

This is a smart tank car capable of voice-controlled hazard prevention. Upon powering on, it enters a standby state. The WonderLLM large model supports controlling the robot's movement using voice commands. During line following, when the ultrasonic sensor detects an obstacle in front within 20 cm, the car automatically stops, while the controller triggers a buzzer alarm and starts the fan to cool the area. Like an intelligent safety monitor, it automatically completes environmental monitoring and emergency response tasks.

3.32.2 Learning Objectives ​

  1. Understand 360° block motors, the 270° block servo, the ultrasonic sensor, the 4-channel line follower sensor, the fan module, and the large AI model, mastering coordinated wiring and programming.
  2. Master voice-controlled movement, ultrasonic audio-visual warnings, and automated ventilation upon obstacle detection to simulate smart operations.

  • Connect the right 360° block servo to port S2 of the micro:bit expansion board, ensuring the yellow wire of the servo is inserted into the white pin of S2.

  • Connect the 270° block servo controlling the fan to port S4 of the micro:bit expansion board, ensuring the yellow wire of the servo is inserted into the white pin of S4.

  • Connect the 270° block servo controlling the right hand to port S5 of the micro:bit expansion board, ensuring the yellow wire of the servo is inserted into the white pin of S5.
